work_package_routes.title: Bootstrap runtime and evidence workspace
work_package_routes.rationale: The offline roster and evidence layout are bounded, reversible, and validator-backed, while T2 review protects against credential leakage or falsely qualifying an unavailable runtime.

work_package_routes.title: Lock module, schema and command contracts
work_package_routes.rationale: This package fixes schema ownership, command authority, three-valued logic, and effect boundaries that every later package consumes, so both contract authorship and review require T1.

work_package_routes.title: Create runnable repository and isolated development stack
work_package_routes.rationale: The synthetic-only monolith scaffold is reversible and deterministically checked by lockfile, build, dependency, startup, and credential-isolation tests, with T2 review for environment-boundary mistakes.

work_package_routes.title: Implement human authentication and server authorization
work_package_routes.rationale: Authentication, bootstrap, step-up, RBAC, and ActorContext are substantial implementations from locked contracts, but a hidden bypass or first-user takeover requires independent T1 security review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement identity, profiles and endpoint bindings
work_package_routes.rationale: Identity normalization, merging, splitting, and endpoint rebinding are bounded domain implementation, yet errors could transfer permission or erase safety history and therefore demand T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement permission, withdrawal, preference and suppression policy
work_package_routes.rationale: Implementing consent, withdrawal, preference, suppression, and reconsent against approved semantics is T2 work, while any permissive mistake directly expands communication authority and needs T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement typed audiences and safe segmentation
work_package_routes.rationale: The parameterized segment compiler is high-complexity implementation; UNKNOWN, negation, scope, or source-coverage defects can silently include recipients, so max effort and T1 logic/security review remain mandatory.

work_package_routes.title: Implement independent recovery journal and restrictive ingress
work_package_routes.rationale: The journal adapter is a bounded implementation, but its acknowledgement, outage, replay, and restore barriers independently preserve denials and effect evidence, warranting max effort and T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement verified inbound provider events
work_package_routes.rationale: Signed ingress and monotonic event reduction are complex but contract-bounded; invalid, duplicate, or out-of-order events could weaken restrictions, so T1 independently reviews negative and replay paths.

work_package_routes.title: Implement email provider and sender readiness adapter
work_package_routes.rationale: Provider and fake transports are high-complexity adapters, but acceptance-unknown classification, sender scope, suppression, and quota errors can duplicate or misdirect effects and require T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement email content revisions and rendering
work_package_routes.rationale: Renderer and codec work is complex but reversible and strongly verified by pinned revision, fallback, sanitization, and deterministic fixture tests, allowing only a one-step effort downshift with T2 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement delivery plans, atomic coordination and effect executor
work_package_routes.rationale: Atomic reservations, current eligibility, semantic deduplication, permits, retries, and unknown outcomes form the core effect executor; implementation is T2 under settled contracts with mandatory T1 concurrency/recovery review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement forms, confirmation and staged imports/exports
work_package_routes.rationale: Forms, confirmation, and staged data movement are established T2 implementation, but replay, public identifiers, or mappings could invent permission, expose PII, or weaken denials and therefore need T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement audience and message operator workspace
work_package_routes.rationale: The manual CRUD workspace is bounded and reversible with server-scope, keyboard, screen-reader, and deterministic-focus oracles; T2 review covers scope presentation and accessibility consequences.

work_package_routes.title: Implement campaign approval, recipient resolution and lifecycle
work_package_routes.rationale: Campaign snapshots and lifecycle are complex bounded implementation, while partial resolution, stale approval, scheduling, cancellation, or uncertain completion defects can create unauthorized effects and require T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement proposal, preview and approval foundation
work_package_routes.rationale: Proposal, revision, diff, and approval services implement settled exact-envelope semantics, but stale or self-approved consequential actions would expand authority, making max effort and T1 review necessary.

work_package_routes.title: Implement metrics, operational dashboards and workload harness
work_package_routes.rationale: Instrumentation and rollups are high-complexity implementation because counters distinguish communications, interruptions, attempts, cost, weak evidence, and stale sources; T1 review guards operational and causal overclaims.

work_package_routes.title: Qualify sender, renderer and first email release
work_package_routes.rationale: This package adjudicates real sender, renderer, security, restore, canary, and accountable-owner evidence before the first live release, so both evidence assembly and independent review require T1.

work_package_routes.title: Inventory Kit and prove migration topology
work_package_routes.rationale: Although discovery is read-only, interpreting incomplete Kit topology, status classes, cursor evidence, legacy links, and cross-publication coupling defines later migration authority and needs T1 evidence reasoning and review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement migration staging, fencing and authority transfer
work_package_routes.rationale: The approved migration state machine is T2 implementation, but freezes, drains, checkpoints, authority epochs, negative reconciliation, and repair-forward rollback prevent dual sends and require T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Migrate the first publication and observe
work_package_routes.rationale: Executing the first live authority transfer and judging canary, legacy opt-out, observation, and rollback evidence is irreversible and externally consequential, requiring T1 authorship and review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement single durable workflow runtime
work_package_routes.rationale: A single durable executor is high-complexity T2 implementation, while cursor, wait/timeout, replay, cascade, and provider-acceptance races can lose or duplicate effects and mandate T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement restricted sequences and enrollment
work_package_routes.rationale: Sequences are bounded atop the shared runtime, but version pinning, reentry, withdrawal, reconsent, and migration-position errors can restart or rewrite recipient work and need T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement bounded event-driven automations
work_package_routes.rationale: Typed automations and their simulator are complex T2 implementation, while UNKNOWN conditions, waits, replay, loops, and actions could create permission shortcuts or unbounded effects and require T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement portfolio administration and contextual preferences
work_package_routes.rationale: Portfolio reuse and contextual preferences are T2 implementation, but cross-brand visibility, shared identity, fairness, and broader preference views could pool authority or leak relationships and demand T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Refine human UX, search, Inspect and attention views
work_package_routes.rationale: Search, resumption, Inspect, and attention views are bounded reversible UX work with offline, stable-label, keyboard, and screen-reader verification; T2 review protects accessibility and authority legibility.

work_package_routes.title: Implement goals, scoped preferences and interaction context
work_package_routes.rationale: Goals, persistent preferences, and explicit session context are T2 implementation, while hidden memory, stale patches, or ambiguous workspace references could silently alter authoritative state and need T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement built-in textual assistant
work_package_routes.rationale: The assistant is a bounded proposal layer, but context assembly, invalid model output, PII, cost, grants, safety blocks, and deterministic fallback cross security and authority boundaries requiring T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement external-agent principals and delegation
work_package_routes.rationale: Delegation sessions are substantial implementation against explicit contracts, while attribution, scope, revocation, human-only approval, budget, and kill-switch failures could transfer authority and require T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Expose structured external tools and API
work_package_routes.rationale: The API and optional thin MCP are high-complexity exposure of existing commands, but discovery filtering, authentication, revision binding, idempotency, and approval parity are security boundaries needing T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement voice-forward interaction
work_package_routes.rationale: Voice is complex integration over the textual assistant, while provisional transcription, ambiguity, microphone privacy, retention, cancellation, and mode handoff can create unintended authority or disclosure and need T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Qualify computer use and agent/expert surface
work_package_routes.rationale: This is an adversarial qualification of computer use, stale state, restricted delegation, stop behavior, and human-only approval rather than routine UI implementation, so T1 must author and independently review the evidence.

work_package_routes.title: Qualify interaction release and accessibility
work_package_routes.rationale: Release qualification synthesizes red-team, privacy, vendor, accessibility, outage, operator, AI, agent, and voice evidence with a zero-invariant-breach condition, requiring T1 on both sides.

work_package_routes.title: Roll out portfolio publication by publication
work_package_routes.rationale: Each remaining live publication transfer requires fresh topology, cursor, legacy-negative, workflow, observation, owner, and rollback judgments, so repeated execution does not reduce it below T1.

work_package_routes.title: Implement bounded onsite placements
work_package_routes.rationale: Onsite placement is bounded T2 channel implementation, but personalization, tracking inference, shared devices, caching, expiration, and outage behavior can expose data or bypass consent and require T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement qualified web push
work_package_routes.rationale: A single qualified push use case is bounded T2 implementation, while endpoint secrets, device multiplicity, permission versus consent, withdrawal, quiet hours, and replacement behavior need T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Implement approved cross-channel plans
work_package_routes.rationale: Cross-channel routing is complex T2 implementation from approved semantics, but equivalence, pressure, preference, opt-out, complaints, unknown acceptance, and races could multiply or evade effects and require T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Qualify multi-channel recipient experience
work_package_routes.rationale: The evidence determines whether broader non-email activation is justified and must distinguish recipient value from extra volume while assessing pressure, accessibility, reliability, and incident ownership, requiring T1.

work_package_routes.title: Qualify optional phone or app channels
work_package_routes.rationale: Choosing whether a phone or app channel is feasible joins actual demand, market law, provider rules, consent, replies, geography, cost, and product-scope constraints, so T1 authorship and review are necessary.

work_package_routes.title: Implement operations and production runbooks
work_package_routes.rationale: Runbooks and deployment machinery are high-complexity implementation, while secrets, migrations, journal access, rollback, restore, and an independent send fence have production safety consequences requiring T1 review.

work_package_routes.title: Perform independent core security and invariant review
work_package_routes.rationale: Independent attacker-boundary review integrates authorization, rendering, ingress, dependencies, and external effects and can hold the release for critical findings, so the review package itself remains T1 with T1 verification.

work_package_routes.title: Run restore, failure and workload qualification
work_package_routes.rationale: Restore and failure qualification must reason across PITR, independent journal replay, post-backup denials, accepted-before-crash uncertainty, RPO/RTO, and load isolation, demanding T1 authorship and review.

work_package_routes.title: Release selected mature platform profiles
work_package_routes.rationale: The mature-profile release decision reconciles exact artifact identity, applicable must-pass evidence, optional-profile boundaries, owner sign-off, maintenance, incidents, and outstanding brand gates, requiring T1 throughout.

work_package_routes.title: Evaluate triggered infrastructure optimization
work_package_routes.rationale: Measured replacement of provider, queue, analytics, cache, workflow, or service boundaries is an architectural cost/reliability decision that must preserve authority and recovery semantics, so it remains T1 despite a high risk label.

notes: T1-T4 are coding capability tiers, separate from Texenda product command consequence classes C0-C4.
Every whole-parent route defaults to max. No current parent is wholly mechanical enough for a T4 floor; a weaker-capability subtask needs a separately reviewed plan/policy addition.
Allowed profiles are policy eligibility, not current runtime availability. Exact profiles require fresh owner-attested evidence.
Consequence sets a capability floor before effort selection. Escalate effort first unless consequence or scope requires a stronger floor.
